title: Controls made of rows over a table of radios, a fieldset of radios, checkboxes and a file input
blurb: Four controls from the ui-feed collection that are stacks of rows, rebuilt around native elements: a waterfall of a page loading with a radio in each row, a list of playback speeds, a list of flavours and a list of files that share out the height.
question: Can the canvas reshape the picture of an ordinary list of rows (squeeze it, scale it, cut it in two) and keep every row's native input under the finger?
result: Yes in the test browser. Numbers were squeezed to 60% of their width, rows were scaled to fit the height with their buttons moved to the right edge, and the bars of a waterfall were drawn over a table of radios. All four took taps on an emulated phone and stopped painting at rest. Nothing here is verified on a phone.
